scope: Conversational adaptation of supplied Click procedural material, official public Foundation/Design Sprint guides, and the saved combined Character board. Not full Sprint-book, Click-bonus-pack, podcast, or unframed-canvas coverage.

activities.title: Set the stage
activities.prompt: Who decides, who contributes, and what constraints shape the work?
activities.output: Roles, scope, workspace, working agreement and schedule
activities.completion_check: Real Decider identified; team roles and conversation/solo adaptations explicit

activities.title: Use independent generation and decision
activities.prompt: What options emerge before discussion or convergence?
activities.output: Independent options, inputs/votes, and reasoned Decider choices
activities.completion_check: Independent human work preserved where available; AI perspectives labeled; votes inform rather than bind

activities.title: Choose the target customer
activities.prompt: Which specific people should we help first?
activities.output: Selected customer statement and alternatives
activities.completion_check: Identifies real reachable people; unresolved audience claims labeled

activities.title: Choose the customer problem
activities.prompt: What actual struggle occurs, apart from this proposed feature?
activities.output: Selected problem statement
activities.completion_check: Customer problem distinguished from a preferred implementation

activities.title: Examine founding advantages
activities.prompt: What can we unusually do, understand, and care about?
activities.output: One capability, insight, and motivation with basis
activities.completion_check: All three represented; conviction separated from customer evidence

activities.title: Map current alternatives
activities.prompt: What do people use now, including workarounds and doing nothing?
activities.output: Basics sheet with 3–5 alternatives and toughest competitor
activities.completion_check: Basics joins customer/problem/three advantages/competition; assumptions and observations distinguished

activities.title: Explore differentiating dimensions
activities.prompt: What can we deliver that customers would perceive as different?
activities.output: Classic/custom scales and selected pair
activities.completion_check: Consider eight Click scales and custom scales; select two with reasons; hypothesized customer value labeled

activities.title: Compare competitive positions
activities.prompt: Do these axes honestly distinguish us from the strongest alternatives?
activities.output: 2x2, competitor placements, and reality check
activities.completion_check: Do not fabricate superiority to get an empty quadrant; revisit axes/approach when unsupported

activities.title: Write the Mini Manifesto
activities.prompt: Which practical rules protect the promise and the customer?
activities.output: Values, about three principles, and differentiation chart
activities.completion_check: Actionable principles cover differentiation and harmful-success concern; wording and source variant recorded

activities.title: Generate alternative approaches
activities.prompt: How else could we solve this, including if our favorite failed?
activities.output: Candidate set and selected approaches
activities.completion_check: Use Click checklist3–7 options, preferring4+ when meaningful; preserve alternatives and chosen count

activities.title: Make each option understandable
activities.prompt: What is its value and how would the experience work?
activities.output: One-page title/value sentence/doodle per option
activities.completion_check: Comparable summaries explain customer/problem/differentiation; rough sketches are sufficient

activities.title: Expose comparison criteria
activities.prompt: Which positive qualities make each option promising?
activities.output: Identified options and criteria pool
activities.completion_check: Silent/independent review and 1–4 criteria per option, or documented solo adaptation

activities.title: Compare the four classic lenses
activities.prompt: How do options compare for customers, delivery, growth, and value?
activities.output: Customer, pragmatic, growth, money charts
activities.completion_check: All four assessed; axes/placements/reasons explicit; noncommercial substitutions labeled

activities.title: Add project-specific comparisons
activities.prompt: Which tradeoffs are missing from the standard lenses?
activities.output: Additional charts and differentiation comparison
activities.completion_check: Use checklist2–4 additional charts plus differentiation; selected custom axes and tradeoffs explicit

activities.title: Choose a top bet and backup
activities.prompt: Where do the charts agree or disagree, and what matters most?
activities.output: Decider choice of one top bet and backup
activities.completion_check: Decision cites tradeoffs, contradictions, and judgment; no invented universal total score

activities.title: Write the Founding Hypothesis
activities.prompt: Why should these people choose this approach over alternatives?
activities.output: Conditional founding hypothesis and scorecard questions
activities.completion_check: Connects customer/problem/approach/competition/differentiation; customer/switching/click claims remain testable

activities.title: Prepare the Design Sprint
activities.prompt: Which challenge, roles, and study resources are needed?
activities.output: Decider/facilitator/contributors, challenge, schedule and workspace
activities.completion_check: Role and time adaptations explicit; recruiting and interview ownership assigned

activities.title: Set the goal and observable success
activities.prompt: What future result matters and what would show progress?
activities.output: Long-term goal, metrics, and trial-specific success questions
activities.completion_check: One optimistic goal without numeric targets or prescribed solution; separate 2–3 rough numeric metrics; not commitments or measured results

activities.title: Choose crucial risks
activities.prompt: What could prevent the goal, and which uncertainties must this test address?
activities.output: Answerable risk questions, two selected risks, and consolidated goal/metrics/risks
activities.completion_check: Important risks selected with rationale; other risks retained; miniature predictions about selected solutions follow the sketch decision

activities.title: Map actors, discovery, and core experience
activities.prompt: How do the relevant actors find the offer and reach the value?
activities.output: Actor set, discovery and core journeys, outcome event, target customer/moment/risk
activities.completion_check: Current/imagined steps distinguished; HMWs mapped; selected target risk may revise earlier priorities

activities.title: Learn from expertise and frame opportunities
activities.prompt: What do informed people know that changes this map?
activities.output: Expert input, organized How Might We notes, selection and revised map
activities.completion_check: Source default 2–4 real experts, organized HMWs and 3–7 selected for map; actual sources/people distinct from AI; absent human input requires pending/adapted status, never invented interviews

activities.title: Collect useful solution patterns
activities.prompt: What can we learn from other products without copying irrelevant detail?
activities.output: Pattern examples and implications for this target
activities.completion_check: Examples documented; relevance explained rather than treated as demand evidence

activities.title: Explore independent solutions
activities.prompt: What distinct solutions could answer the target question?
activities.output: Notes, ideas, Crazy8s and solution sketches
activities.completion_check: All four sketch stages represented or explicit adaptation; alternative solutions remain intelligible

activities.title: Select prototypes and mini hypotheses
activities.prompt: Which sketches best address the risk, and why should they work?
activities.output: Heat-map/critique/straw-poll inputs, Decider selection, and two focused mini hypotheses about selected solutions
activities.completion_check: Chosen solution/comparative prototypes fit capacity; mini hypotheses follow selection and connect predictions to goals/metrics/risks

activities.title: Plan the test experience
activities.prompt: What must a participant see and do from entry to outcome?
activities.output: Storyboard with realistic copy/content and test flow
activities.completion_check: Flow includes discovery/context and value; scope sufficient for the question without production build

activities.title: Recruit appropriate participants
activities.prompt: Who actually fits this customer and how will we screen and confirm them?
activities.output: Recruitment owner, screener, schedule and confirmations
activities.completion_check: Default five screened target customers; record board variant or single-user adaptation explicitly

activities.title: Build a realistic simulation
activities.prompt: What fidelity allows a credible response to the selected question?
activities.output: Testable prototype, production roles and integrated trial run
activities.completion_check: Required flow works in rehearsal; simulated backend and feasibility limits explicit

activities.title: Prepare the customer study
activities.prompt: How will neutral prompts reveal the participant experience?
activities.output: Interview guide, observation grid and study logistics
activities.completion_check: Welcome/context/introduction/tasks/debrief; no leading sales pitch; scorecard links to hypotheses

activities.title: Observe real customer sessions
activities.prompt: What do the screened participants actually do and say?
activities.output: Individual session records and scoped observations
activities.completion_check: Actual participants/results required; retain recruitment/context/count and contradictions; no synthetic replacements

activities.title: Review patterns and scorecard
activities.prompt: What worked, failed, surprised us, or remains unclear?
activities.output: Scorecard, observation patterns, hot takes separated from evidence
activities.completion_check: Actual customer-study observations support the scorecard and interpretations; template preparation is not synthesis; preserve uncertainty and dissent

activities.title: Assign next work after the customer study
activities.prompt: What should we change, test, build, pause, or stop?
activities.output: Post-study decision and assigned actions with outcomes and dates/triggers
activities.completion_check: Decision follows actual customer observations and synthesis, with bounded investment and unresolved risks. An initial session handoff cannot complete this post-study activity.

activities.title: Consider head-to-head comparisons
activities.prompt: Would comparison with another approach, competitor, workaround, or status quo resolve an important uncertainty?
activities.output: Comparison plan/results or a reasoned applicability decision
activities.completion_check: Comparison considered explicitly; if performed, separate observed preference from switching/payment claims

activities.title: Review iteration and reuse
activities.prompt: What changed across the recommended three Design Sprints, and what should we do next?
activities.output: Cycle history with hypothesis revisions, reused/changed work, observations and decisions
activities.completion_check: Default Foundation plus three Design Sprints accounted for with actual results; fewer cycles require an explicit adapted status and evidence/scope rationale, or leave pending on early stop; no fixed number proves success
